The edges with exactly one end in S are B–D, C–D and C–E, in accent and labelled with their edge ids. The call returns those ids, 4, 5 and 6." width="100%"} The edge boundary of `S` is every edge with exactly one end in `S` (with `T=`, edges between `S` and `T`). On a directed graph, only edges leaving `S` count, as in NetworkX's `edge_boundary()`. These are the edges a cut would remove; their number (or total weight) is `cut_size()` on undirected graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optionally only count edges ending in these nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the boundary edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only the bridge leaves the first triangle: ::: {#e0f5ecd2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) ends = graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id label = graph.get_label_from_id [[label(n) for n in ends(e)] for e in graph.edge_boundary(["A", "B", "C"])] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [['C', 'D']] ``` ::: :::
